title: SpecLook: Speculating Where to Look for Fast and Reliable Agentic MLLMs
description:
arXiv:2611.23483v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that think with images interleave reasoning with zoom-in tool calls. However, this sequential loop is slow, and its answers carry no reliability score. Prior speculation of tokens, reasoning steps, or answers keeps the loop, and answer speculation also accepts confident errors. title: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents
description:
arXiv:2611.23588v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enterprise LLM agents operate in dynamic environments where foundation models evolve rapidly, workflows update frequently, and deployments need to satisfy accuracy and cost requirements. We propose ARISE (Agent Refinement through Iterative Self-Evaluation), a practical memory architecture in which the agent's memory evolves from its own failures without updating model weights, tools, or workflow logic. description:
arXiv:2611.23751v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous LLM agents incur substantial cost and latency by invoking a large model (System-2) at every step, even when many intermediate actions choose among a small set of known candidates. Existing dual-system agents offload such decisions to a lightweight System-1 model, but rely on workflow-specific hooks authored per environment. title: Metrics-in-the-Loop: Complexity Feedback Reshapes Agent-Written Code
description:
arXiv:2611.23817v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding agents now write whole codebases in long autonomous runs, guided mainly by whether their tests pass. Yet passing tests alone does not reveal accumulating complexity or gaps in test coverage, which then persist as agents extend their own code. description:
arXiv:2611.23910v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The typical workflow for improving large-scale ranking and recommendation models is slow and tedious: an engineer forms a hypothesis, implements it as a code change, trains a model, and evaluates it both offline and online, often relying on their own intuition and experience along the way. title: BOS Summary: The First Token Matters
description:
arXiv:2611.23508v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) and language models (LLMs) often exhibit attention sinks, whereby particular positions, such as the beginning-of-sequence (BOS) token, receive a disproportionate share of attention. Under standard causal masking, however, the BOS query attends only to itself, so the representation that later tokens repeatedly access carries no information about the input. description:

Abstract: In cosmology, surveys span different sky regions and wavelength ranges, resulting in uneven modality coverage across observational datasets. description:
arXiv:2611.23678v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous agents that run ML experiments are usually judged by the best score they reach. That score says nothing about how it was reached: whether the agent stayed within the files it was allowed to edit, whether failed trials were kept or silently dropped, and whether each keep or discard decision can be traced to its evidence. description:

description:
arXiv:2611.23824v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning from terminal answer rewards enables search-augmented language models to interleave reasoning and retrieval without step-level annotations, yet outcome supervision assigns identical credit to every search in a trajectory regardless of whether it retrieved useful information. title: A System 1 Decision Model for Medical Multiple-Choice Questions Built on Frozen Language Models
description:
arXiv:2611.23832v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A System 1 model answers a multiple-choice question in a single pass. A frozen language model turns the question and each option into vectors, two small, trained heads place them in a shared space, and the closest option wins. description:
arXiv:2611.25269v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generative AI is becoming embedded in knowledge work as an intelligent collaborator to assist in completing tasks. title: Intelligent Embedding Pruning for Large-Scale Recommendation Models
description:
arXiv:2611.25288v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern recommendation systems face substantial memory pressure, largely from the sparse embedding layer that maps high-cardinality categorical features into dense vectors. In-training embedding pruning (ITEP) removes less important embedding rows during training, yielding end-to-end memory savings but sometimes degrading accuracy because per-table pruning ratios are set by size-based heuristics. description:
arXiv:2611.24959v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: The rise of powerful, fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) necessitates robust natural language inference (NLI) systems. title: Infer3D: Inverse Generative Modeling Enables Robust 3D Reconstruction
description:
arXiv:2611.25061v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Humans can understand the 3D structure of scenes even from highly unfamiliar or extreme viewpoints. Cognitive science suggests this generalization stems from a top-down generative inference strategy. In contrast, state-of-the-art 3D reconstruction neural networks typically rely on amortized, feedforward inference.
